eventTypes.title: Community Events
eventTypes.summary: Health fairs, senior centers, and sponsored community education where Medicare products may be discussed only within permitted scopes.

eventTypes.title: Retail Booths
eventTypes.summary: In-store or kiosk environments with defined hours, signage, and traffic flow; heightened visibility requires strict script and material controls.

eventTypes.title: Carrier Events
eventTypes.summary: Co-branded or carrier-hosted forums; follow carrier-specific addenda plus CMS marketing and communication standards.

eventTypes.title: Self-Hosted Events
eventTypes.summary: Sessions you or your agency organize; you own permits, notices, scope-of-appointment capture, and post-event documentation.

allowed: Educational presentations that stay within approved talking points and materials.
Collecting permission-to-contact when all required disclosures are delivered first.
Scheduling follow-up appointments in compliant channels after SOA is documented.
prohibited: Cash, gift cards, or meals conditioned on enrollment.
Health screening positioned as a requirement to hear a sales presentation.
Discussing off-scope products before scope and disclaimers are complete.
disclaimers: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Medicare or the federal government.
Plan availability and benefits vary by county; network and formulary rules apply.
We do not offer every plan available—contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE for options.
soaRules: Scope must list which product types may be discussed (e.g., MA, PDP, ancillary).
Document consent before needs analysis tied to a specific plan sale.
For new contacts, retain compliant evidence of permission to contact and scope.

allowed: Fixed scripts and leave-behinds pre-approved for the location.
Sign-in or QR flows that capture consent disclosures in order.
Referrals to licensed agents for detailed plan comparisons by appointment.
prohibited: Open enrollment discussions without a defined private or semi-private area when required.
Displaying carrier logos inconsistent with written co-marketing approval.
Pressure tactics tied to in-store promotions unrelated to Medicare.
disclaimers: Same government / scope / availability disclosures as other marketing channels.
Recording notice if calls may be monitored or recorded per state policy.
Limited hours and representative licensing shown on posted notice where required.
soaRules: Retail traffic is often cold—obtain explicit scope before personalized recommendations.
If event is only educational, do not pivot to sales without a new SOA pathway.
Document language preference and accessible format needs when captured on-site.

allowed: Activities explicitly listed in the carrier event addendum.
Distribution of carrier-approved collateral with your licensing reflected.
Coordinated RSVP or registration processes reviewed by compliance.
prohibited: Deviating from approved agendas or speaker roles.
Offering incentives beyond carrier-authorized nominal items.
Comparing competitors by name in ways that violate fair communication rules.
disclaimers: Combine CMS-required disclaimers with any carrier mandatory footers.
Clearly state your relationship to the carrier and appointment of record rules.
If PDP/MA dual-eligible topics arise, apply specialized disclosure cadence.
soaRules: Many carrier events still require individual SOA before enrollments.
Batch sign-in does not replace person-specific scope where selling occurs.
Retain carrier attestations alongside your local audit trail.

allowed: Controlled invitation lists with documented marketing approval.
Virtual or hybrid formats using compliant platforms and recording notices.
Post-event surveys that avoid steering language.
prohibited: Exclusive deals framed as one-night-only urgency for Medicare products.
Combining charitable donations with enrollment quotas.
Using purchased leads without verified permission chains.
disclaimers: Event advertising must mirror eventual on-site disclaimers.
Virtual waiting rooms should repeat identity and scope before breakout sales.
Nominal refreshments must meet gift nominal value policies.
soaRules: You are responsible for capturing SOA at the moment discussion turns to sales.
Self-hosted does not relax cold-call rules for follow-up.
Archive attendee lists, scripts version IDs, and slide decks per retention policy.

scenarios.title: Busy health fair table
scenarios.instructions: You have long lines and limited space. Practice a 60-second compliant greeting: permission, disclaimers, and how you will schedule a private follow-up instead of selling at the table. Document what you would write on the sign-in sheet.

scenarios.title: Shopper asks “What’s the best plan?”
scenarios.instructions: Respond without steering: explain that best depends on drugs, doctors, and budget. List the steps you take to confirm SOA before any plan-specific detail. Note one prohibited phrase you will avoid.

scenarios.title: Carrier speaker runs over time
scenarios.instructions: The agenda is compressed. Outline how you still deliver required disclosures before one-on-one sessions. Identify which materials you may defer to a scheduled call.

scenarios.title: Friend brings an uninvited guest
scenarios.instructions: The guest did not receive pre-event marketing. Describe how you treat them as a cold contact: fresh disclosures, permission, and whether you reschedule for a compliant channel.

before: Materials, slides, and giveaways compliance-reviewed and versioned.
Licenses, appointment numbers, and state notices verified for the venue.
Signage, permits, and venue contracts aligned to marketing type.
Staff roles (greeter vs licensed closer) documented.
during: Deliver required disclaimers before scope-specific discussion.
Maintain nominal gift and refreshment rules.
Use only approved scripts for transitions to enrollment.
Log incidents, complaints, or media presence per playbook.
after: Secure attendee lists and SOA records; restrict access.
Submit carrier or FMO reporting within required windows.
Archive photos/booth layouts if used in supervisory review.
Debrief team on near-miss compliance items.
